name: TX-14
label: Likely R

key_factors: No polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Randy Weber: a Republican-leaning district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge against a Democratic challenger with almost no money. Prediction markets price Weber's win at about 95%, consistent with a Likely R rating.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Weber would be the first sign of movement in this low-visibility race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Weber seeks another term in this Gulf Coast-area district that leans Republican by about twelve points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised nearly a million dollars and holding over $900,000 on hand, while Democrat Thurman Bartie has raised only about $27,000 and reports negative cash. No outside groups are spending against Weber.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and campaign resources. Prediction markets give Weber roughly a 95% chance of winning, and the expected margin sits in the mid-teens in Weber's favor, consistent with a Likely Republican rating rather than a fully safe one.
